title_en: Stories of Modern China (5/20): Grandpa's Paper Cuts
note_en: To describe how well or how fast someone does something, Chinese puts 得 after the verb and the description after 得: 小雨剪得很慢 "Xiaoyu cut very slowly," 剪得这么好看 "cut so beautifully." English uses an adverb ("slowly"), but in Chinese the comment comes after the verb, linked by 得, not before it the way 地 works in 静静地剪 "quietly cut."
